chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-'Ala' Bayya' al-Sabiri, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who entrusted a man with wealth. When death approached her, she said to him, 'The wealth that I gave to you is for so-and-so.' The woman died, and her guardians came to the man and said to him, 'There was wealth for our companion, and we do not see it except with you; so swear to us that there is nothing of hers with you.' Is he to swear to them? He said: 'If she was trustworthy in his presence, he should swear to them; and if she was suspected (of owing more), he should not swear, and he should place the matter upon what it was. Indeed, for her from her wealth is one-third.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a deceased woman entrusted money to a man and named a beneficiary before dying?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the evidentiary weight of a dying woman's declaration regarding entrusted wealth, distinguishing between a trustworthy (مأمونة) and suspected (متهمة) status to determine the heir's oath and the final distribution. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that a single reliable testimony from the deceased can establish a debt, yet limits the claim to one-third if credibility is uncertain, preserving the rights of other heirs. This ruling underscores the balance between honoring the deceased's intent and protecting the inheritance rights of the living family members.
